correctness.rationale: Count the arithmetic isomorphism classes separately over each base field, as in the published census; the invariant computed on each is the geometric a-number, not a tally of distinct geometric classes. The plane-quartic sequence identifies H^1(O_C) with H^2(O_P²(−4)), with Čech basis represented by the reciprocals of X^(v_X+1)Y^(v_Y+1)Z^(v_Z+1) for the three degree-one basis vectors v. Frobenius on these representatives takes the p-th power and multiplies by F^(p−1); extracting the surviving basis monomials gives the record’s displayed matrix up to transpose. Cartier duality and invariance of rank under scalar extension and field Frobenius give a=3−rank(H). A fresh exact computation of the supplied coefficients reproduced every per-field row and the totals (179,32,4,0), as well as the four rank-one matrices at (3,5), (9,25), (9,26), (9,27). Their encodings give the stated equations, including the conjugate pair under r↦r³. Invertible H is equivalent to ordinarity; no a=3 excludes a superspecial Jacobian. The published theorem provides completeness and the per-field row counts agree independently with its Table 1.
residual_risks: The independent computation tests the attached transcription, not the upstream Magma files byte for byte. The upstream supplement was not retrievable for a 215-equation comparison. This review relies on the provenance of the furnished coefficients and the published classification for their smoothness, nonisomorphism over each base field and completeness; matching the field counts alone does not prove those facts about the transcription.
One model counts over both F_2 and F_32, as the source notes. The distribution must not be advertised as 215 distinct geometric classes.

value.rationale: The family is an established, finite census of genus-three curves with maximal gonality over their base fields. A geometric p-torsion invariant on every arithmetic class is a natural refinement that is not supplied by the class counts. The identification of all four rank-one exceptions, and exclusion of rank zero, give precise examples and exclusions usable in studying nonordinary Jacobians with this gonality; neither an arbitrary sample nor a routine extraction from a known a-number column would do so.
residual_risks: No full EO, Newton-polygon or p-torsion classification is asserted. Value is judged for the exact invariant and exceptions on the field-specific census.
